request: Our school library wants a simple catalogue of its books. The librarian should be able to add a book with its title, its author and how many copies the library owns. Students should be able to see all the books, and look at one book to see how many copies are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name, and returns it when they are done; a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. When every copy of a book is out, nobody else can borrow it until a copy comes back.
summary:
The library catalogue is built and all 19 tests pass. The data is saved in a file called `library.db` in the project folder.

**Important: set your own librarian password before you go live.** Right now the password is `librarian-secret`, which anyone reading the code can see. To change it, set a setting called `LIBRARIAN_PASSWORD` on the computer that runs the app. Until you do, anyone who knows that default can add books.

**What the app can do:**
- **Add a book** (`POST /books`), librarian only. The librarian sends the title, author and number of copies, along with the password in a field called `X-Librarian-Password`.
  - A wrong or missing password is refused.
  - A blank title or author is refused.
  - The number of copies must be a whole number of at least 1. Anything else is refused.
- **See all books** (`GET /books`): anyone can see the list, with each book's number, title and author.
- **Look at one book** (`GET /books/{bookNumber}`): shows the title, author, total copies and how many are on the shelf right now. The app works out the shelf count itself from the loans not yet returned, so nobody types it in.
- **Borrow a book** (`POST /books/{bookNumber}/borrow`): the student gives their name, and the app records the date and time.
  - A blank name is refused.
  - If every copy is out, the student is told none are available until one comes back.
- **Return a book** (`POST /books/{bookNumber}/return`): the student gives their name.
  - A blank name is refused.
  - The return only works if that student has a copy of *this* book out right now, so a loan can't be returned twice.
  - If a student has more than one copy of the same book out, the earliest loan is marked returned first.

If someone asks for a book number that doesn't exist (to look it up, borrow it or return it), they get a "book not found" message.

As agreed in the plan, there is no way to edit or remove books or to see who has borrowed what. Students are known only by the name they type, so two students with exactly the same name count as one person.

plan.summary: This plan sets up a simple online catalogue for the school library. The librarian can add books, saying how many copies the library owns. Students can see the list of all books and check how many copies of a book are still on the shelf. A student borrows a book by giving their name and returns it when finished. Nobody can borrow a book when every copy is out, and a student can only return a book they actually borrowed. Nothing in your request was unsafe or unrelated, so nothing was left out. Some things to be aware of: (1) To make sure only the librarian can add books, the system will use a secret librarian password. Students will not need one. (2) Students are identified only by the name they type in, so the system cannot check that a student is who they say they are. If two students share the exact same name, the system will treat them as one person. (3) You did not ask for ways to edit or remove books, or to see who has borrowed what, so those are not included. They can be added later if you want them.

data.name: Book
fields: Book number (created automatically, used to point to one specific book)
Total copies the library owns (a whole number, at least 1)

data.name: Loan (a record of one copy being borrowed)
fields: Date and time it was borrowed
Date and time it was returned (empty while the book is still out)

endpoints.does: The librarian adds a new book by giving its title, author and how many copies the library owns. This only works with the librarian password.
Shows the list of all books in the library, with each one's title and author. Anyone can use this.
Shows one book: its title, author, how many copies the library owns, and how many are still on the shelf right now. Anyone can use this.
A student borrows one copy of this book by giving their name. The system records the loan, so there is one fewer copy on the shelf.
A student returns a copy of this book by giving their name. The system marks their loan as returned, so there is one more copy on the shelf.

rules: Only someone with the librarian password can add a book. Anyone else trying is refused.
A new book is refused if the title or the author is missing.
A new book is refused if the number of copies is missing, is not a whole number, or is less than 1.
The number of copies on the shelf is always the total copies minus the copies currently borrowed and not yet returned. It is worked out automatically, never typed in by hand.
Borrowing is refused if every copy of the book is already out. The student is told no copies are available until one is returned.
Borrowing or returning is refused if no name is given.
Returning is refused if this student does not currently have a copy of this book borrowed. Every return must match one of their own unreturned loans.
A loan can only be returned once. After that, it cannot be returned again.
Looking up, borrowing or returning a book number that does not exist is refused with a 'book not found' message.
